target_customer: Originally phone wholesalers and retailers trading used smartphones, later companies buying, tracking and selling IT equipment
problem: Used electronics wholesale ran through social media groups with little price transparency or trust; the current positioning is IT asset tracking, procurement and buyback.
business_model: Marketplace and exchange taking margin on device trades, with asset management software added later
product_category: B2B electronics marketplace and IT asset management

founders.name: Joshua Nzewi
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2023 says the founders were wholesalers who claimed to have sold $8M of devices in their first two years in the space.

founders.name: David Iya
founders.background_notes: Listed as co-founder on the YC page and in TechCrunch 2023.

competitors.name: Back Market
competitors.what: Consumer refurbished electronics marketplace, an adjacent model rather than a direct B2B rival; not named by Eze

technical_complexity.rationale: A marketplace with escrow, listing and grading flows is standard software; the harder parts are logistics, device grading and cross border trade.

defensibility.rationale: Liquidity among dealers could create network effects, but traders can move back to WhatsApp or other platforms.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No evidence found that incumbents copied or bought Eze; TechCrunch 2023 says traders used WhatsApp and WeChat before Eze.

market_need_then: Used phone traders closed deals in social media groups with little price transparency per a 2020 feature seen in search results; Eze later reported over 500,000 devices facilitated by mid 2023.

branding.domain_note: Moved from eze.co style branding to ezeit.ai for the IT focus; dates not found.

identity.logo: A visual identity refresh exists on a Behance showcase but is not described
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and operational, all in one hub for IT

brand_strength.rationale: Short name but shared with Eze Software and other companies; no brand coverage beyond funding news.

pivots.from: B2B exchange for used smartphones (Eze Wholesale)
pivots.to: IT asset management, procurement and buyback for companies
pivots.why: Not stated; inferred from the current ezeit.ai site and YC description versus the 2020 to 2023 coverage

outcome_analysis: Eze began as a B2B exchange for used smartphones aimed at dealers in markets such as Nigeria and Mexico, raised a $3.7M seed in June 2023 and later repositioned toward IT asset management and procurement for companies. The founders came from the wholesale trade, which fits the problem. The company is active and the reason for the shift is not public.
notes: Founding year conflicts: YC page says 2017, TechCrunch 2023 says 2020, Techloy says 2018; the Eze Wholesale platform launched January 2020 per a search summary of a 2020 feature that was not opened. The TechCabal 2021 article returned 403. Competitor entry for Back Market is an adjacent consumer model and is flagged as such; the main incumbent channel was Computer Village in Nigeria and informal WhatsApp groups, but the sources found are dated late 2020 or later. Nairametrics and other outlets repeat the $3.7M seed. Search for acquisition returned only unrelated companies named Eze (Eze Software, Eze Castle). Lesson applied: no stage labels beyond those stated.
